newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil corn crop seen back to pre-drought levels.
newsitem.headline: Brazil corn crop seen back to pre-drought levels.

text.p: Brazil's 1996/97 corn crop should see a good recovery to 33.6 million tonnes from the drought-hit 30.5 million tonnes collected in 1995/96, said independent analysts Safras e Mercado.
This year's crop will bring production back in line with 1994/95 when the country produced 33.05 million tonnes of corn.
The increase this year is mainly due to higher output from Rio Grande do Sul, the country's second largest producing state which should see a crop of 5.6 million tonnes.
This is after the state produced only 3.26 million tonnes in 1995/96 after a severe drought sharply reduced the crop from the 5.47 million tonnes produced in 1994/95.

This year's crop is also seen higher in expectation of a good "safrinha" or mid-crop in states such as Sao Paulo and Parana where farmers are expected to plant a good area first with soybeans and then corn in the second half of March.
"I think farmers are more likely to plant corn after soybeans than after wheat," said Safras' Paulo Molinari.
The wheat harvest in Parana has been delayed, with the result farmers are now more likely to plant soybeans after letting the land lie for 30 days instead of risking planting late corn, he added.
However the gain to soybeans would be minimal as only five percent of land planted with wheat normally is then used for corn production, he said.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
